title: Eight Chapters
hookLine: his introduction to Pirkei Avot, on the soul's health
last: CRESCAS AND ALBO ARGUED FROM INSIDE, AND STAYED.

cards: Sweet tastes bitter. Bitter tastes sweet. A person with a sick body, Maimonides writes, can lose their sense of taste so badly that they crave what harms them and turn away from what would heal them.
He knew bodies. He worked as a physician. But in this passage he isn't writing about the body.
He's writing about the soul. And he says the same thing happens there. Today, the little book where he says it, written as a doorway into Pirkei Avot.

teach.h: THE SOUL CAN BE WELL OR UNWELL.
teach.b: Shemonah Perakim. Eight Chapters. Maimonides wrote them as an introduction to Pirkei Avot, the Mishnah's tractate of sayings about how to live.
Before he explains the sayings, he wants you to understand the one who will practice them: the human soul. Take it in steps. First, the soul has health and sickness, just like a body.
A healthy soul tends toward good actions and finds them natural. A sick soul tends toward harmful ones, and, like the sick tongue, may even call them sweet.
Second, a sick person needs a doctor, and doesn't trust their own cravings.

teach.h: THE WISE ARE PHYSICIANS OF SOULS.
teach.b: So too, he says, a person whose soul is unwell should go to the wise, who are physicians of souls, and let them help.
Third, the cure is practice. Traits are changed the way health is restored: by doing, again and again, until a new habit takes hold. Pirkei Avot, read this way, is a book of medicine.
Fourth, where he gathered it. In his introduction he says plainly that these ideas aren't all his own.

teach.h: HEAR THE TRUTH FROM WHOEVER SAYS IT.
teach.b: He drew on the sages and on the philosophers, and he tells the reader to hear the truth from whoever says it. A physician uses the remedy that works, whoever found it.
That's the doorway into Avot: not a rulebook, a clinic.

how: Shemonah Perakim is studied as an introduction to Pirkei Avot, a text some communities read chapter by chapter on Shabbat afternoons between Passover and Shavuot, and some through the summer.

o: eight chapters of prayers for healing the sick

the eight chapters of the tractate Pirkei Avot

p: practice, until a new habit holds

s: the Eight Chapters are about the health of the body
Maimonides uses the body as a picture, but the subject is the soul.
he says to hear the truth from whoever says it
he tells the reader he drew on the sages and the philosophers.
for Maimonides, a person with an unwell soul can trust their own cravings
like a sick tongue, the soul may call harmful things sweet; he sends them to the wise.

games.q: you're sick, and everything that would heal you tastes bitter. what does Maimonides say to do?
o: trust your taste and eat what's sweet.
go to a physician, and for the soul, to the wise.
games.why: he says a sick soul, like a sick body, needs a physician: the wise, who are physicians of souls.

practice: Think back over the last few days: is there a habit of the heart that keeps showing up, impatience, worry, a quick tongue? Don't scold yourself; name it plainly, the way you'd say a knee is sore.
Then ask, gently, when it flares up.
